text: The access event DOCUMENT_SEARCH of a search is one append to the service's local decision-record chain through the DP-03 library, written in the request path and published on rwb.decision-record.v1 for the central ledger in rwb-decision. The record carries the caller, the role codes, the criteria with the free text term as its SHA-256 hash, the result count and the case IDs returned, and its record code is taken from the library's own code set at build time. The confirmation AC9 waits for is the library's acknowledged append; an unacknowledged append answers 503 with MSG-P5-019 and releases no row. The key of the record is the caller reference, because a cross-case search has no single caseId.
why: FEAT-ACA-08 puts the access log into the append-only decision log and DP-03 makes that log local, so the record has to be the library's. No source names the record code of an access event, gives it a key for a non-case subject, or states what the 'confirmation' of the legacy PII access log is; each is recorded rather than typed as a business value.

text: The four search parameters SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS = 1000, SEARCH_PAGE_SIZE = 50, FREE_TEXT_MIN_CHARS = 3 and FREE_TEXT_MAX_CHARS = 100 are read through the parameters contract and client library of rwb-case (DP-06), and the rows they resolve to are held in document_hub_parameter in rwb_document, which the Ownership Map gives to P5. The values are the ones the legacy story carries and are marked assumed (DL11); the story types none of them in code.
why: DP-06 sends every parameter read through the rwb-case contract while the document-hub parameter table stays P5's own table, exactly as the delivered sibling stories of this service read the intake parameters. The legacy story reads the table directly and marks the values as assumed, so the values are copied and only the path changes.

text: The case IDs in the caller's scope and their case numbers are read from the case-list operation of rwb-case, GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream, with a fake from Day 1; an empty filter means scope ALL. An answer that does not arrive within 2 s answers 503 with MSG-GEN-006 and no case is searched, because a scope that cannot be read is never treated as ALL. The C row RWB-P3-E1018-CON for that read is not in the Work Package rows.
why: The default ruling gives the case list to P3 rwb-case and DP-11 requires the legacy in-process scope call to become a contract read with a mock. Reading a scope from a case table would break DP-01, and defaulting to ALL when the read fails would show a case outside the caller's scope, which BR1 and CTL-09 forbid.

text: The masking decision of the legacy mayReadUnmasked call is asked of rwb-access through POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise (RWB-P4-E1037-CON), one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker, with a fake from Day 1; the field classes are PARTY_NAME, ACCOUNT_NO and ID_NO and the answer carries the masking version. The guard library of DP-08 is the one the service template already carries and this story builds none of it. The C row RWB-P4-E1037-CON is not in the Work Package rows and DP-08 is not among the patterns.
why: DP-11 turns the in-process masking call into a contract read, and the authorise operation is the one the sibling stories of this service already consume. The service holds no masking rule of its own, and taking the rule from a copied masking table would break DP-01 and put a personal-data decision in the wrong service.

text: DP-15 is met by one step in the per-service Flyway sequence of rwb_document, V1033_1__document_search_indexes.sql, which creates the pg_trgm extension, the trigram index on document_text(text_content), the function dochub_to_numeric and the two document_field indexes. The step adds no table and no column and reuses the case/type/date index that RWB-P5-E1024-APP creates; the extension privilege is part of the login grant of RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and the accept date and version number follow the sequence in force.
why: The legacy migration V1_5_033 is a step of the monolith baseline that DP-15 replaces with a per-service sequence, and the four search objects are still needed for AC1, AC3 and AC7 to answer inside the budget. Creating a table would add a second copy of an index the service already owns.

text: A search publishes no business event of rwb-document, starts no workflow and owns no Schedule: it is a synchronous read that consumes committed rows. DocumentStored (EV-16) and the intake events (EV-17) remain the published events of this service and belong to the store, the intake and the extraction slices; the only thing a search publishes is its access record on rwb.decision-record.v1.
why: The Work Package lists no DP-09 and no DP-10 pattern, the legacy story declares 'None' in its state-transition section and writes no record of its own, and a read that emitted a business event would put a personal-data query on a business topic for no consumer.
